title: Link Hierarchy Key Chips to Table of Contents
description:
Every hierarchy key chip (the number chip drawn next to a heading title — section, subsection, subsubsection, paragraph, appendix, nested paragraphs — and every other chip rendered through the shared hierarchy-number renderer) must become a hyperlink that jumps to the matching line in the Inhaltsverzeichnis (TOC).

This is the reverse direction of the already-clickable TOC rows (which link TOC line -> section). Implementation: emit a per-line anchor in \SemioTableTocRow (print/tex/semio-table.sty) keyed by the hierarchy number, and wrap \semio_hierarchy_chip_number:n (print/tex/semio-core.sty) — the single choke point used by \semio@kind@number, \semio@kind@number@bare and \semio_kind_chip_number:nn — in a guarded \hyperref that degrades to plain text when no TOC line exists for that number (windows, first compile pass). Guard against duplicate anchors. Verify by building the print templates and inspecting the PDF link annotations / destinations.
summary:
Every hierarchy key chip is now a hyperlink that jumps to its own line in the Inhaltsverzeichnis — the mirror image of the already-clickable TOC rows.

New `TocLineLinks` region in `print/tex/semio-core.sty` holds both halves, keyed by the hierarchy number itself (a heading chip is typeset long before or after the TOC body exists, so it cannot know the TOC's own label names — but it always knows its number):
- `\semio@tocline@anchor{<number>}` drops a `\phantomsection\label{semio-tocline-<number>}` destination, guarded by a seen-set so a repeated number (unnumbered front-matter chapters all carry `0`) never duplicates the destination.
- `\semio@tocline@link{<number>}{<content>}` wraps chip content in `\hyperref` when that label resolves, and falls through to plain content otherwise, so window slots (`1.2.a`) and the first compile pass never emit a dangling destination. Robust (`\NewDocumentCommand`) because project cards carry their key through `\protected@edef` and a further `\edef` before it is typeset.

`\semio_hierarchy_chip_number:n` — the single choke point behind `\semio@kind@number`, `\semio@kind@number@bare` and `\semio_kind_chip_number:nn` — now wraps its output in that link, so section/subsection/subsubsection/paragraph/appendix heading pairs and hand-numbered nested paragraphs all link with one change. Its explicit `\textcolor` calls keep the muted-head/bright-tail colouring intact against hyperref's `colorlinks`.

`\SemioTableTocRow` (`print/tex/semio-table.sty`) emits the anchor in the number cell, after `\cellcolor` as colortbl requires. Project cards bypass the shared renderer (`\semio@window@header@number` is `\let` to a raw `\thesubsection`), so a new robust `\semio@project@key@chip` attaches the link there and restates the muted `semio-chrome-text-normal` tone that colorlinks would otherwise override.

Verified by rebuilding all six print templates (light + dark) and mit-bestand/bericht/zwischenbericht, then reading the PDFs' link annotations and named destinations with `inspect_links.py` (in the ticket folder): every `/GoTo` annotation resolves, destinations land on distinct y-positions one TOC row apart, and every TOC line has exactly one chip pointing at it — 245/245 in the real Zwischenbericht (both themes), 8/8 in report, 7/7 in the zukunftbau Zwischenbericht. The only unlinked TOC lines are forschungsbericht's two unnumbered front-matter chapters ("Förderhinweis", "Kurzbeschreibung / Abstract"), which draw no key chip at all. No "multiply defined" or undefined-reference warnings in any log. Rendered page comparisons confirm chip colours are byte-for-byte unchanged.

Out of scope and left alone: `bunx nx run print:test-quick` fails on a pre-existing stale assertion at `print/script.ts:689`, which still expects `\vskip\dimexpr-3\semio@stroke@hairline` while the untouched `semio-window.sty:436` reads `\vskip\dimexpr-\semio@stroke@hairline-5.75pt`. The remaining source-shape assertions on `semio-table.sty` were re-checked by hand and still match.
